chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad said:

I hired a donkey to go to Qasr Bani Hubayra and return, for such and such a price. I set out in search of a debtor of mine. When I reached near the bridge of Kufa, I was informed that my companion had headed towards the Nile, so I headed towards the Nile. When I reached the Nile, I was informed that he had headed towards Baghdad, so I followed him and caught up with him. I settled what was between me and him, and returned to Kufa. My going and returning took fifteen days. I informed the donkey owner of my excuse, and I wanted to release myself from him regarding what I had done and to please him, so I offered him fifteen dirhams, but he refused to accept. We agreed based on Abu Hanifa's ruling. I told him the story, and the man told him. He said to me, 'What did you do with the donkey?' I said, 'I returned it sound.' He said, 'Yes, after fifteen days?' He said, 'What do you want from the man?' I said, 'I want the hire of my donkey, for he detained me for fifteen days.' He said, 'I do not see that you have a right, because he hired it to Qasr Bani Hubayra, but you diverted it, so you rode it to the Nile and to Baghdad. He guaranteed the value of the donkey, and the hire fell due. When he returned the donkey sound and you took it, the hire did not bind him.'

He said, 'So we left his presence, and the donkey owner was making du'a for him (restraining). I had mercy on him because of what Abu Hanifa had ruled, so I gave him something and released myself from him. I performed Hajj that year, so I informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what Abu Hanifa had ruled. He said, "In a ruling like this and its like, the sky withholds its rain and the earth withholds its blessing."'

He said, 'So I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you think?' He said, "I see that he has a right over you equal to the hire of the donkey going from Kufa to the Nile, and equal to the hire of the donkey from the Nile to Baghdad, and equal to the hire of the donkey from Baghdad to Kufa, and you must pay it in full to him."'
He said, 'I said, 'May I be your ransom, I had fed it with dirhams, so the feed is for me over it.' He said, "No, because you are a usurper (ghasib)."'
I said, 'What do you think if the donkey became lame or died, would it not be binding upon me?' He said, "Yes, the value of a donkey on the day you diverted it."'
I said, 'And if the donkey suffered a fracture or old age or a defect?' He said, "Upon you is the value of the difference between soundness and the defect on the day you return it to him."'

I said, 'Then who knows that?' He said, "You and he. Either he swears on the value and it becomes binding upon you, and if he returns the oath to you and you swear on the value, that becomes binding upon you. Or the donkey owner comes with witnesses who testify that the value of the donkey when it was hired was such and such, and that becomes binding upon you."'

I said, 'I gave him dirhams and he was pleased with them and released me.' He said, "He was pleased and released you when Abu Hanifa ruled against him with injustice and oppression. But return to him and inform him of what I have ruled for you. If he makes you free after his knowledge, then there is nothing upon you after that."'

Abu Waddad said, 'So when I returned from that journey, I met the hirer, and I informed him of what Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had ruled for me. I said to him, 'Say what you will until I give it to you.' He said, 'You have made Ja'far ibn Muhammad dear to me, and preference for him has occurred in my heart. And you are free. And if I want to return to you what I took from you, I will do so.'

key_terms.غَاصِبٌ: Usurper (one who takes rights without full entitlement)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Abu Hanifa's ruling and Imam al-Sadiq's ruling regarding a hired animal that is diverted from its agreed route?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential divergence between the Hanafi school and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding *ijarah* (leasing), specifically addressing whether deviation from the agreed route voids the hire or merely requires compensation for the time used. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the hirer becomes a *ghasib* (usurper) of the animal's utility, entitling the owner to full hire for the actual path taken and liability for any depreciation, thereby correcting the Hanafi view that sound return sufficed. The narrative underscores the Shia principle that mutual consent based on a flawed legal ruling (*ghurur*) does not fully absolve the debtor until the correct obligation is acknowledged and paid.
